name: Roshni Lulla
title: Co-Founder and Head of Research
bio: Roshni is a cognitive neuroscientist who studies how emotion and moral values shape decisions, and applies that work to AI safety. Her research bridges affective neuroscience, moral cognition, and AI misalignment. She is Co-Founder and Head of Research at the Institute for Humane Robotics, where she works on guidelines for safe human-robot interaction, and a co-organizer of SIRA. She holds a PhD in Brain and Cognitive Sciences from the University of Southern California, where she was advised by Antonio Damasio and Jonas Kaplan at the Brain and Creativity Institute.

name: Muhua Huang
title: PhD Student
discipline: Psychology, Cognitive science, Sociology, Organizational behavior
bio: Muhua is a PhD student studying Computational Social Science at Stanford University and a member of the Stanford-Berkeley Computational Culture Lab. Muhua's research treats AI systems as active social participants, studying culture, values, cognition, and individual differences in AI using psychometric and computational social science methods. Muhua has previously conducted research on AI evaluation as a Student Researcher at Google DeepMind and on AI alignment at Microsoft Research Asia.
directions: Evaluating the social and psychological properties of AI systems (e.g., personality, cognition, social behavior) | Value and safety evaluation, and alignment of AI systems
example_project: Psychometric validation of AI ‘personality’: a fellow would administer established personality or value inventories to several LLMs under varied prompts and personas, then test whether the responses show the same factor structure, reliability, and measurement invariance seen in human samples. The second stage would test predictive validity, asking whether trait scores predict how the same models behave as agents in downstream tasks such as negotiation or workplace simulations.
methods: Psychometrics and measurement (scale development, factor analysis, SEM) | LLM evaluation and benchmarking | Generative agent-based simulations | Computational text analysis and embeddings | Survey experiments
looking_for: Fellows with an academic research background in psychology, sociology, cognitive science, or computer science, who have interdisciplinary interests and a clear sense of what they want to pursue.
mentoring_style: Remote. A weekly 30–60 minute meeting plus async communication on Slack.

name: Alex Csaky
title: Astra Fellow
bio: Alex is an AI safety researcher working on AI for epistemics and decision-making: how AI can help people form better beliefs, make wiser decisions, and coordinate. Alex co-authored a report on the state of the field of AI for epistemics and coordination, and is now looking at how to put these tools to use in the real world. Alex studied archaeology and anthropology at the University of Oxford and is interested in how anthropology's research methods and goals can be applied to AI safety and to navigating toward good futures.
directions: AI for epistemics and decision-making | Putting AI tools for epistemics and coordination to use in the real world | Applying anthropological research methods and goals to AI safety
